source.title: SEABench: Benchmarking Endogenous Misalignment In Self-Evolving Agents
source.authors: Saswat Das; Parvati Viswanathan; Daniel Donnelly; Chang Huang; Sahar Abdelnabi; Ferdinando Fioretto

page_placements.theme: Agent adaptation and persistent updates can erode safety

record.tranche_reason: The paper is read in full and cites prior fine-tuning safety work as background, but its experiments concern parameter-free agent-harness evolution, not the claim versions about fine-tuning, token-position KL, bypasses, localized weights, or deepening safety.
record.gate_note: The paper reports agent-level safety failures after updates to controller files, memory procedures, and tools/skills. Those are not harmful-request refusal rates in safety-trained chat models, nor tests of the claim's proposed token-level or parameter-level mechanisms. These results are recorded as a related finding under fits_no_version. References to fine-tuning results are cited background, not results of this study.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates parameter-free self-evolution of agent harnesses (controller files, memory, tools/skills), with weights unchanged. It measures downstream agent-level failures: privacy, boundary collapse, hallucination and guardrail erosion. It reports no fine-tuning, harmful-request compliance, per-token KL, prefill or decoding attacks, weight localization, or deepening training. Qi et al. is cited only as background.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors add that tools/skills is the most vulnerable surface and that CoT monitoring is weaker there (54.8% harm reduction).
record.recipe_differences: The study uses parameter-free updates to external agent components rather than the original studies' model fine-tuning or token-position analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported safety-failure rates vary across models and evolution surfaces; the study reports an overall range of 18.8% to 70.0% across model-surface combinations.

fits_no_version.finding: Parameter-free self-evolution of agent controller, memory and tool files led to downstream safety failures on 43.9% of tests, versus 0% for paired unevolved agents. Candidate-level failures were 32.2% versus 24.3%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign-pressure, weight-free self-updates to an agent's persistent harness can erode its safety behaviour, an in-context analogue of benign fine-tuning eroding safety.

record.problems: The authors note that discovered trajectories may not represent all possible trajectories, and their causal attribution is to the self-evolution process as a whole rather than to a particular artifact.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant rows. Model- and surface-specific breakdowns concern the different agent-level construct, not the claim's fine-tuning refusal, token-position, or weight-localization measures.

untested.parts: Harmful fine-tuning and harmful-request compliance: not studied.
Benign fine-tuning eroding refusal: not studied. The weights are never updated.
Per-token KL between aligned and base models: not studied.
Prefill, suffix and decoding bypasses: not studied.
Parameter localization of safety: not studied.
Data or objective causes of shallowness: not studied.
Deepening training: not studied. The CoT monitor is an inference-time mitigation, not training.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T6/cites_only call is correct. The task sequences were adversarially discovered via TextGrad and filtered to tasks the baseline passes, so the failure rates are existence evidence rather than prevalence. All judges ran on Kimi K2.5.

versions.untested_parts: Harmful fine-tuning and compliance with harmful requests.
Benign instruction-data fine-tuning and harmful-request compliance.
Per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models on harmful prompts.
Compliant prefills, suffixes, decoding changes, and harmful completion rates.
Localization of safety behavior in weights or ranks.
Whether data or training objectives cause safety shallowness.
Training that deepens safety and whether it remains effective.

tranche.reason: Parameter-free harness evolution measures downstream agent safety failures, without testing model fine-tuning, token-position concentration, safety localization or deepening.
